header.name: Maya Chen
header.headline: COO Candidate | Scaled Operations to IPO | International Expansion at Speed

tailored_summary: I am a COO with track record of building the operating systems that take Series C scale-ups through IPO and beyond. At FieldGrid, I reduced cost-to-serve by 47 percent over four years while revenue grew four times, launched into six new markets in eighteen months, and led the company through its 2023 IPO. Earlier at Verdant, I restructured operations to handle a five times larger book of business with the same headcount and led the company through a US PE acquisition. I prefer building over running. I run what I build until it can run itself. I am writing because the role description matches the kind of work I want to be doing for the next three to five years.

competencies.label: Scaled Operations and Cost-to-Serve
competencies.evidence: Built and ran the operating system at two scale-ups through their highest-growth phases. Specific track record of reducing cost-to-serve while headcount and complexity grew. Reduced support cost per ticket by 47 percent at FieldGrid while transaction volume quadrupled. Restructured the operations team at Verdant to run a 5x larger book of business with the same headcount.

competencies.label: International Expansion and Market Entry
competencies.scale_marker: launched into 7 markets across EU, APAC
competencies.evidence: Led market entry into the Netherlands, Germany, France, Spain, Singapore, Australia, and Japan across two roles. Built the legal, finance, payroll, and customer support stack for each market. Verdant's Singapore office reached profitability within nine months; FieldGrid's Germany expansion hit 40 percent of UK revenue within eighteen months.

competencies.label: Public-Market Readiness and Compliance
competencies.evidence: Stood up the financial controls, audit committee, and operational reporting systems that took FieldGrid through its 2023 IPO readiness review. Same role at Verdant in 2018, though that company was acquired before listing. Comfortable working with Big Four audit firms and dealing with SOX-equivalent requirements.

competencies.label: Executive Team Build and Coaching
competencies.evidence: Hired and onboarded 14 VPs and Directors across both COO roles, including the CFO, CRO, CMO, and General Counsel at FieldGrid. Built the leadership operating cadence (weekly, monthly, quarterly), coaching plans for new VPs, and the performance management framework used across leadership.

competencies.label: Data-Driven Operations and Reporting
competencies.scale_marker: rebuilt the metrics stack at both companies
competencies.evidence: Rebuilt the operational metrics stack at both companies. At FieldGrid, replaced eleven scattered dashboards with a single board-grade reporting suite. The board adopted these metrics as the basis for all operational reporting. Comfortable with NetSuite, Salesforce, Workday, and Tableau; can specify what good looks like to a data team.

competencies.label: M&A and Post-Merger Integration
competencies.evidence: Led integration of three acquisitions at FieldGrid totalling £85m enterprise value. Took the Verdant business through its acquisition by a US PE firm in 2019 and was retained for the integration. Specific experience reconciling tech stacks, harmonising customer success motions, and managing redundancies cleanly.

cover_letter.opening: I read the Series C announcement last month and the line that stood out was the bet on European expansion before US scale. That is the same call FieldGrid made in 2021, and the next three years there shaped how I think about international operations at this stage. I am writing because the COO role you have advertised is the work I want to be doing for the next three to five years.
cover_letter.career_fit: I have built the operating systems for two scale-ups through their highest-growth phases. At FieldGrid, that meant taking a first-COO brief from Series C through IPO. At Verdant, it meant readying a Series C consumer fintech for a US PE exit. The Lumen role looks like the same shape of work in a sector I have not operated in directly, but where my experience with regulated international expansion translates closely.
evidence: Two specific things I would bring. First, the cost-to-serve work. At FieldGrid I reduced support cost per customer by 47 percent over four years while transaction volume grew four times, by consolidating eleven tools to four, restructuring customer success around segment ownership, and investing in self-serve product. The Lumen JD calls out gross margin pressure as a 2026 priority; this is the work I have done before. Second, the international expansion. I launched FieldGrid into six new markets in eighteen months, including two of the markets Lumen is targeting (Singapore and Germany). I know the failure modes.
cover_letter.closing: I would value an early conversation to understand what 18 months of progress would look like in the role and where the operational pressure points are now. I am free for an exploratory call any morning next week.
